A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HoloLLM work. Their full text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–D support comparison, with retained material matched across layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original recognition, question-answering, captioning, ablation, and fusion results on MM-Fi and XRF55 in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds fusion comparisons and Audio/UWB evaluation results in Appendix C, Tables 7–8.

M1.justification: Appendix C.3 adds weighted-sum and max-pooling token-fusion procedures alongside the existing concatenation approach. These are limited inference variants; the core UMIP architecture, encoders, training objectives, and two-stage training strategy remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix C.4 and Table 8 extend evaluation to Audio and UWB inputs for recognition and Action QA, citing SAMOSA and SleepPoseNet as their sources. This adds two sensor/data domains beyond the retained MM-Fi and XRF55 coverage, although the new datasets' experimental details are sparse.

E2.justification: Table 7 adds weighted-sum and max-pooling fusion alternatives to comparisons involving single modalities and naive concatenation. The main Tokenpacker, Honeybee, OneLLM, and ImageBind comparator set is unchanged. Newly cited LanguageBind is not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added fusion experiments specify weights of 0.8 for Vision and 0.2 for mmWave/Infrared. Existing splits, sample sizes, metrics, backbones, and training schedules remain unchanged. Splits and data/training budgets for the new Audio/UWB evaluations are not specified, so changes to those settings cannot be established.

E4.justification: Appendix C.3 extends the existing fusion analysis to test whether weighted sums or max pooling avoid the QA and captioning degradation seen with concatenation. The original encoder/UMIP ablations, token visualizations, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The additional tables retain the existing practice of reporting scores without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 7–8 add distinct fusion and new-modality result sets: weighted fusion gives MM-Fi QA 81.4 versus concatenation's 66.4, and Audio recognition is 63.94 for HoloLLM versus 37.71 for Baseline. Table 2 revises OneLLM Random caption METEOR for Infrared/RFID/WiFi from 1.7/1.5/2.0 to 13.7/11.6/13.7. Tables 2–3 revise HoloLLM CrossEnv XRF55 WiFi QA from 4.5 to 2.7 and its average from 12.8 to 12.4; Table 6 still reports 4.5.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, UMIP equations, and training losses in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about HoloLLM, UMIP, the benchmark construction, and improvements of up to approximately 30%. The appendix additions do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C.3 now interprets weighted fusion as effective for QA and captioning, extending v1's discussion of concatenation failures. New C.4 attributes efficient adaptation to additional modalities to UMIP and pretrained modality-specific encoders, although it supplies no data-budget analysis. Existing limitations and broader-impact qualifications are unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-repository pointer, updates the project-page address, and documents the fusion weights. Appendix B's implementation and hardware details remain unchanged. Detailed encoders, preprocessing, splits, and budgets for the new Audio/UWB experiments are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds LanguageBind to the prior-art discussion and Figure 3 caption, plus SAMOSA and SleepPoseNet references supporting the additional modalities. The related-work narrative and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are small grammatical edits and a conference-status footer update. Appendix C.3 is renamed from 'Naive Multimodal Fusion' to 'Multimodal Fusion' and expanded, while C.4 and its contents entry are added. The main narrative and section order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8, enlarges several existing main-text figures, and adjusts table sizing and float placement. Table 2's headers explicitly identify Accuracy and METEOR. All 13 existing figures retain their content.

improvement.justification: The added fusion comparison provides useful evidence beyond v1's concatenation failure, while broader sensor results, clearer displays, and a code pointer improve the paper modestly. Revised OneLLM caption entries also agree with their reported average. These benefits are limited by undocumented Audio/UWB protocols and data budgets, which weaken the efficiency interpretation, and the new inconsistency between WiFi QA values in Tables 2–3 and Table 6.
